newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end well bid, Telecom hits all time high.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end well bid, Telecom hits all time high.

text.p: * New Zealand leading shares close strongly bid
* Telecom hits all time high
* Energy Direct among well-sought utilities
Price movements at close.
LAST CHG
331 -1 * NZSC cap index +10.39 at 4,492.73
367 -6 * Volume NZ$73.3 million. Futures 1,130, +5
703 +8 * Other movers - +7 +5
Leading New Zealand shares closed well bid on Tuesday with Telecom New Zealand ending at NZ$7.03, one cent shy of the $7.04 all time high it reached during the session.
Luke Koekoek of brokers JB Were & Son said the shares were marked up well at the opening and traded well through most of the afternoon.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed up 11.55 at 2,243.62.
"Turnover was active at $73.3 million indicating overseas guys are in our market and quite content," Koekoek said.

"There is a lot of each way business going through which is encouraging. Telecom and Brierley Investments were the feature. There is still a lot of unsatisfied offshore buying out there (in Telecom) which is defying gravity."
Telecom ended at an all time closing high of $7.03 after going ex a 9.5 cent dividend on September 9. Brierley Investments added three cents to $1.44.

Koekoek said among the Fletcher letter stocks, Fletcher Building had been under pressure lately but the worst seemed to be over and it was finding "encouraging support". The stock closed up three at $3.23.
Fletcher Energy, also up three at $3.53, was benefiting from demand for oil stocks since the Iraq troubles and was getting a spin-off from higher oil stocks in the United States.

"Lion Nathan (off six cents at $3.67) was again one of the underperformers and I feel it is the absence of a large buyer in the market more than anything else. Locals feel it is fully priced and there is an overhang of selling out there so there might be some more selling come out in Lion," Koekoek said.
Outside the leaders, Energy Direct was up seven at $3.25.

TransAlta New Zealand, the vehicle for the proposed merger of Wellington power companies Energy Direct and unlisted Capital Power, today lifted its forecast profit for the March 1998 year to $24.7 million from $22.57 million.
-- Vernon Small 64 4 4714 278
